sections.h2: What a Pinellas tax bill covers
sections.html:
The tax collector counts 495,057 accounts on the 2026 roll, worth more than $2.75 billion, divided among 56 local taxing authorities, including the school board, the county commission, the cities and libraries. The appraiser lists 437,624 real property parcels, 408,947 of them residential, from condo towers to manufactured home communities. Whatever you own, you deal with the same two offices.

Three kinds of charges can show up on one notice. Ad valorem tax follows value. Tangible personal property tax covers furniture and equipment in businesses and rentals. Non-ad valorem assessments are fixed amounts for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue and solid waste, and they do not depend on value.

The appraiser keeps ownership and mailing addresses, and the collector says it does not maintain them. If no bill arrives in November, call 727-464-7777 or search the collector's database. A notice that never came does not excuse payment.

The cutoff depends on how you pay. Online payments run until 11:55 pm Eastern on the last discount day. Counter and drop box payments stop at closing time, and a mailed check needs a postmark from that month.

If a discount month ends on a weekend or holiday, paying online or in person the next business day keeps the discount.

• Online eChecks carry no fee but cannot be used for delinquent bills. Credit and debit cards add a 2.5 percent vendor fee.
  • Checks by mail go to P.O. Box 31149, Tampa, FL 33631-3149. The collector warns that USPS now postmarks at a regional processing facility, so a late drop in a local box may miss a deadline.
  • Drop boxes sit outside select offices, and paying at an office needs no appointment.
  • Multiple checks must travel in one envelope, and a check that bounces is handled by a recovery partner that may re-present it with a fee.

An online payment shows as paid at once in the collector's system, though a bank can take up to five business days to reflect it. For 2026, bills went out beginning October 30. Online payment opens November 1, and counter and mail payment opens November 2.

Owners with an estimated bill above $100 can pay in four installments, which earns a discount of roughly 3.5 percent overall. Applications for the 2027 plan open November 1, 2026 and run through April 30, 2027.

  • June 30: one quarter of last year's total, discounted 6 percent.
  • September 30: another quarter, discounted 4.5 percent.
  • December 31: a quarter plus half of any adjustment, discounted 3 percent.
  • March 31: a quarter plus the other half of the adjustment, with no discount.

A June payment missed can still be made by July 31 without the discount, and missing July 31 removes the account. A late second or third payment rolls into the next one and loses its discount. Once enrolled, you do not reapply each year as long as the first payment arrives.

Under a partial payment plan, an owner pays current-year tax in pieces of at least $100, but only until March 31, and the early payment discounts are lost. Delinquent bills are not eligible. The 2026 application stays open through March 31, 2027, and a balance unpaid by May 31 goes to a certificate sale.

Deferral suits homestead holders, since it rests on the prior year's household income. The collector stresses that deferral creates a lien and that deferred tax accrues interest every month. The 2026 application deadline is March 31, 2027, and the office answers at 727-464-3409.

The collector said Amendment 3 would not change 2026 bills, and that any change would begin with the 2027 tax year. Afterward, the Pinellas Property Appraiser's home page reported updating its website for the amendment's passage. If you are giving a buyer a tax estimate for next year, look at the appraiser's updated exemption pages first.

The county courthouse office is at 315 Court Street, 2nd Floor, Clearwater. North County is at Northside Square, 29269 US Hwy 19 North, Clearwater. Mid County shares space with the tax collector at 13025 Starkey Rd, Largo, and South County is at 2500 34th Street North, 2nd Floor, St. Petersburg. The main line is (727) 464-3207, answered on weekdays.

Ask the collector for a payoff so the closing agent can settle it from proceeds. Delinquency begins April 1, and the collector lists its 2027 certificate sale for Friday, May 28, 2027, with online payments of 2026 taxes accepted until 5:00 pm on May 27. The title agent clears any certificate.

The buyer's reassessment will not follow your old bill, and a homestead sale ends the cap, though portability may help your next home.

If a certificate was already sold on the parcel, the payoff will include it, and the title agent will want the redemption amount in writing with a good-through date. Ask for a fresh figure if the closing date moves, because interest and fees change the total from week to week.

Keep every receipt. A paid-in-full printout from the collector is the cleanest proof you can hand to a buyer or a lender.

sections.h2: A year of the tax calendar, from a seller's side
sections.html:
Late October: bills are mailed, and the discount clock starts in November. November through February: each month you wait costs one percentage point, so a seller expecting to close soon can often save money by paying early and settling up with the buyer at the table. March: the full amount is due by March 31. April 1: the bill turns delinquent and the account stops being eligible for online payment. May: unpaid current-year balances move toward the certificate sale.

Closing dates rarely line up with that calendar. If you close in the middle of a discount month, ask the title agent whether paying the bill first makes sense and how the buyer will reimburse you for their share of the year.

Start by searching the parcel on the collector's site to see what is paid and what is open. Request a written payoff that matches your expected closing date, and ask the title agent to confirm it. If you used an installment plan, deferral or partial payment arrangement, tell the title agent right away, since each one affects the figure at closing.

Give your buyer the appraiser's parcel record instead of your own bill as a guide to next year's taxes. Bills for owners of long standing often sit far below what a new owner pays, so your number may mislead.

Whether you list the house or sell for cash, expect the lien to be settled from the sale proceeds and ask the closing agent for a settlement statement that shows the tax line.

faqs.q: Which office handles the Pinellas bill?
faqs.a: The tax collector mails and collects it. The property appraiser sets value and keeps the mailing address.

faqs.q: What is the 2026 Pinellas November discount?
faqs.a: It is 4 percent. December is 3, January 2 and February 1, with no discount in March.
The collector says about 3.5 percent overall, with discounts of 6, 4.5 and 3 percent on the first three quarters.

faqs.q: Can I make partial payments in Pinellas?
faqs.a: Yes, in amounts of at least $100 before April 1, but early payment discounts are lost.

faqs.q: Does Amendment 3 touch the 2026 Pinellas bill?
faqs.a: No. The collector said any change would begin with the 2027 tax year.
